nodes.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be continuous on $[a, b]$, where $a \le b$ and $f(a) \le 0 \le f(b)$, and let $u, v$ be a bisection sequence for $f$ from $a$ to $b$. Then there is $c \in [a, b]$ with $f(c) = 0$ such that the midpoints $(u_n + v_n)/2$ converge to $c$ and $|(u_n + v_n)/2 - c| \le (b - a)/2^{n+1}$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.
nodes.title: Bisection method converges at a linear rate

nodes.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be continuous on $[a, b]$, where $a \le b$ and $f(a) \le 0 \le f(b)$. Then there is a bisection sequence $u, v$ for $f$ from $a$ to $b$ such that for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$: $u_n \le u_{n+1} \le v_{n+1} \le v_n$, $v_n - u_n = (b - a)/2^n$, and $f(u_n)\,f(v_n) \le 0$.
nodes.title: Bisection method: nested intervals

nodes.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ and $a \le b$ with $f(a) \le 0 \le f(b)$. Then there is a bisection sequence $u, v$ for $f$ from $a$ to $b$ such that for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$: $u_n \le u_{n+1} \le v_{n+1} \le v_n$, $v_n - u_n = (b - a)/2^n$, and $f(u_n)\,f(v_n) \le 0$.
nodes.title: Nested bisection intervals from a sign bracket

nodes.summary: For every function $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ and all reals $a$, $b$, there are sequences $u, v$ forming a bisection sequence for $f$ from $a$ to $b$.
nodes.title: Existence of bisection sequences

nodes.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ and $a \le b$ with $f(a) \le 0 \le f(b)$, and let $u, v$ be a bisection sequence for $f$ from $a$ to $b$. Then for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ we have $a \le u_n \le v_n \le b$ and $f(u_n) \le 0 \le f(v_n)$.
nodes.title: Bisection invariants

nodes.summary: For a function $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ and reals $a$, $b$, two sequences $u, v : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}$ form a bisection sequence for $f$ from $a$ to $b$ when $u_0 = a$, $v_0 = b$, and for every $n$, writing $m_n = (u_n + v_n)/2$ for the midpoint, either $f(m_n) \le 0$, $u_{n+1} = m_n$ and $v_{n+1} = v_n$, or $f(m_n) \ge 0$, $u_{n+1} = u_n$ and $v_{n+1} = m_n$.
nodes.title: Bisection sequence

nodes.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$, let $a \le b$, and let $u, v$ be a bisection sequence for $f$ from $a$ to $b$. Then $a \le u_n \le v_n \le b$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.
nodes.title: Bisection intervals stay inside the initial interval

nodes.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$, let $a \le b$, and let $u, v$ be a bisection sequence for $f$ from $a$ to $b$. Then for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, $u_n \le u_{n+1} \le v_{n+1} \le v_n$.
nodes.title: Bisection intervals are nested

nodes.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$, let $a, b$ be real, and let $u, v$ be a bisection sequence for $f$ from $a$ to $b$. Then $v_n - u_n = (b - a)/2^n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.
nodes.title: Length of the bisection intervals

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
